# Housekeeping: wasm-gate-guest

## Authorized scope and smallest closable slice

Review the complete `tools/wasm-gate-guest` Cargo package and its tests. Deliver practical, behavior-preserving cleanup in this package, or an evidenced no-change verdict when existing choices earn their cost. Cover all five user requests: repeated code/LoC; load-bearing test purposes; avoidable copies; applicable micro SIMD; and data structures that cap efficiency. The user requests two GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh agents concurrently; this overrides the default Terra implementation model for this workflow. Root Sol owns briefing, adversarial review, exact-path checkpoints, integration and remote synchronization.

## Frozen boundaries

Existing public APIs, feature behavior, canonical/wire identities, arithmetic order and per-lane rendered bits, latency/tail, link modes, smoothing and NaN/denormal rules remain contractual. Zero render allocations/frees, locks, I/O or syscalls; no runtime native ISA dispatch. Retain scalar tails, 4-lane Wasm/NEON and x86 AVX2/FMA. Preserve all feature and target configurations. Do not expand another open issue or change DSP algorithms. Read current related issue bodies before touching their subject; discoveries that require architecture or product decisions become bounded follow-ups and final owner questions.

## Implementation and test-value decisions

Prefer deleting or consolidating repetition to adding abstractions that increase total complexity. Assess every existing test or a clearly named homogeneous family by its plausible unique defect; remove trivial, redundant or obsolete cases only after identifying the surviving behavioral gate. Keep independent numeric/oracle, fault, allocation, queue, boundary and target tests. Add/rewrite tests only for a concrete uncovered defect, and state which plausible defect no existing test catches. No prose/source-grep tests, new bit-digest pins or exact resource-byte pins. Copies needed for ownership, snapshots or atomic admission stay unless the same semantics are proved with less work. Data structure changes must preserve deterministic order and bounded realtime work. Inspect applicable hot loops and generated code before claiming additional SIMD; recursive/stateful dependencies alone do not justify changing arithmetic.

## Objective gates and evidence

- Read all production and test files in this package; record concise findings for each of the five requests, concrete changed/deferred locations, and load-bearing test families with retained coverage for deletions.
- Run focused locked package tests and affected feature configurations; use existing downstream/RT/differential gates proportional to the changed contract. Check formatting and package clippy with warnings denied. Relevant Wasm and AArch64 compile checks are required for changed product code; record limitations candidly.
- Changes to DSP arithmetic or hot state need existing independent numeric and scalar/SIMD gates plus one-time base/head evidence when needed; no permanent comparison against the old implementation. Existing research remains the algorithm authority; no new algorithm or listening claim is authorized.
- Benchmarks are optional and descriptive. Any timed measurement freezes its workload/validator, passes zero-workload preflight, and runs exactly one invocation with one warmup/two measured rounds. No timing optimization loop, performance percentage or unsupported sound-quality claim.
- Root conducts one adversarial verdict per coherent attempt, at most five total attempts. Every new/rewritten test gets its unique-defect sentence in that verdict. No-change audits require the same five-axis review, not manufactured edits.
- Stop after a coherent compiling, focused-green tranche; root commits exact owned paths before further edits. Keep edits within `tools/wasm-gate-guest` and this numbered spec. Independent crates use separate worktrees. Root pushes promptly and updates this GitHub issue with evidence; close only after PASS and evidence upstream, verifying remote state. Merge through the required qualification check and remove clean completed worktrees.

## Attempt evidence

### Attempt 1 — full audit, documentation-only correction

Worker B (GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh) read the complete 232-line Rust file, manifest, all eleven exports, cache/bounds/probes, their Wasmtime reader and existing opcode-census owners. Related #172, #952, the current single-owner corpus/target rulings and the separate #1173 source record were reviewed. Root approved only stale documentation corrections, checkpointed `tools/wasm-gate-guest/src/lib.rs` as `b68c1845`, and integrated/pushed through `d8d32fa2`. The intro now correctly identifies the shared corpus's native `rlib` and this guest's `cdylib`-only role, with the runtime dependency in `wasm-gates`; lane-case and f64 comments describe the actual delegated families and supported SIMD128 lowering. Net Rust **−1 line** (9 added/10 removed). Every executable expression, export, cache/probe and manifest is unchanged.

Five-axis findings:

- **Repetition/LoC:** each metadata/count export is a short direct boundary adapter. The two xorshift probe loops have different finite/raw-word inputs and independently named function bodies that the existing lowering census must inspect; factoring them would add an abstraction/call boundary without a justified reduction. Only the inaccurate comments earned cleanup.
- **Test value:** there are no local test functions or generators to retire. The actual guest's shape, valid digest ABI, raw-word mismatch counts and two separately censused SIMD probes have distinct downstream owners described below. No test/harness/pin was added or rewritten, and no scenario was deleted.
- **Copies/ownership:** the one-entry cache owns a 32-byte digest. Returning its small array copy releases the mutex guard before the export decodes/checks its requested word, without exposing a reference to mutable cache storage. Misses compute before replacing the entry; hits match both case and width. Preserve the lock, poison recovery, case/width-before-word validation order and all original allocation lifetimes. The probe scratch/output arrays are already fixed and bounded; their gather/fold words keep computations observable. No unnecessary large copy was found.
- **Micro SIMD:** the f64 probe exercises widen/mul/add at Simd4; the full-meter probe exercises the actual browser meter kernel over raw hostile words and folds every output field. Their `#[inline(never)]` exports and unchanged arithmetic earn their direct lowering checks. Reused actual guest disassembly confirms both vector censuses; no new SIMD algorithm, spill or performance claim is justified.
- **Data structures:** `Mutex<Option<Cached>>` is bounded to one result and amortizes the host's eight consecutive word reads without a growing lookup table. The lock is tooling synchronization, outside the engine render callback; replacing it with unsynchronized storage would change the thread/ownership contract. Fixed scratch arrays and primitive `u32` ABI results need no alternate structure.

ABI/cache/probe family purposes (all retained):

- `miso_gate_case_count`, `miso_gate_lane_case_count`, `miso_gate_widths`, `miso_gate_lane_width`, `miso_gate_backend` report the corpus and actual compiled lane types. The host validates corpus shape, expected backend and exact `[1, 4]` lane widths, so scalar-oracle duplication or a missing vector width cannot pass by matching pins alone. The leading-lane-count export is preserved ABI metadata; the current reader does not call it, and no runtime check of that export is claimed.
- `miso_gate_digest_word` and its case/width-keyed cache transfer all eight little-endian words through the pointer-free ABI. The host reconstructs the 32-byte digest and compares every applicable case/width to the sole shared pins. Cache ownership stays internal and instance-local; no reference or scratch pointer escapes. Existing valid-word execution covers repeated cache hits and transitions between case/width keys, but does not claim poison injection or hostile argument refusal coverage.
- `miso_gate_minmax_lowering_mismatches`, `miso_gate_f64_lane_mismatches`, `miso_gate_meter_block_mismatches` expose three independent zero-count gates for raw NaN/zero/min-max lowering, integer-oracle widening/binary64 operations/energy chains and independent scalar full-meter fields. Digest agreement cannot replace those hostile-word comparisons.
- `miso_gate_f64_lane_probe` and `miso_gate_meter_block_probe` give the script two specific bodies to census. The first requires packed f64 promote/mul/add instead of scalar conversion/arithmetic; the second also requires vector peak/count operations and refuses scalar f32 add/gt/abs. Output folds prevent dead elimination. This is disassembly qualification, not a claim that the host directly invokes these probe exports at runtime.
- The host instantiates with an empty import object, resolves typed exports, iterates valid cases/widths and requests words `0..8` exclusive. Native G5/G6 separately own shared-corpus parity, nonvacuity, finiteness and caller FP-environment contracts. This guest adds no second pin table, engine entry point or render loop.

Actual qualification and limits:

- Current `cargo clippy --locked -p wasm-gate-guest --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `check-workspace-policy.sh`, `check-lane-policy.sh`, `check-realtime-policy.sh` and `git diff --check` all PASS. Logs: `/tmp/engine-housekeeping-b-1149/{clippy,fmt,workspace-policy,lane-policy,realtime-policy}.log`; builds used the existing private target directory. No compiler warnings/errors were reported.
- Reused #1148 actual shipping SIMD128 guest execution is valid because all executable guest source is identical: **142 cases / 250 comparisons**, no digest mismatches and minmax/f64/meter mismatch counts all **0**, using pinned Wasmtime 47.0.3. Detector residency scanned seven limiter functions. Both named probes contain two vector promote/mul/add operations and no scalar f64 substitutions; the full meter also retains vector abs/count adds. No guest rebuild or duplicate runtime/target matrix was performed for these comments.
- Verified preserved artifacts outside this worktree: `/tmp/engine-housekeeping-b-1148/wasm-gate-guest.simd128.wasm`, `wasm-gate-guest.simd128.dis`, `wasm-gates/wasm-gates.jsonl`, and `wasm-simd128-gates.log`. Those are the #1148 build/runtime artifacts, not newly built comment-change bytes. #1148's native debug G5 (7) and release G5/G6 (7 + 2) remain the actual shared-corpus execution evidence. No empty local test run, descriptive workload, timing, new harness or dependency change was manufactured.

**Separate source-only finding #1173:** on wasm32, release `(word as usize) * 4` can wrap before `offset + 4 <= digest.len()`. For word `0x40000000`, the source arithmetic selects offset zero instead of the documented out-of-range trap. Root and worker independently confirmed the source/profile/normal host caller and recorded the matched successor `.github/ISSUE_SPECS/1173-reject-oversized-wasm-digest-word-indices.md`. No runtime reproducer or fix was executed, and no implementation is authorized here. Normal host words 0–7 do not exercise this refusal gap; safe slice bounds remain, so this is a tooling ABI contract finding, not an engine or memory-safety claim. Cache/poison/bounds behavior is preserved in housekeeping.

Completion is paused for root's single attempt-1 verdict and remote synchronization. No architecture/API owner decision or additional qualification expansion is requested; disposable builds remain until the final clean worktree removal as directed.
